summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with primary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a suprapubic catheter, was admitted with sepsis secondary to a urinary tract infection. He presented with fever, tachycardia, hypoxemia, and markedly elevated white blood cell count. Initial treatment included IV fluids, Meropenem, and Linezolid, later transitioned to Vancomycin and Piperacillin-Tazobactam before switching to oral Bactrim based on urine culture results showing E. coli sensitive to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. His hypoxemia was attributed to atelectasis, and he was weaned off supplemental oxygen. Speech and swallow evaluation recommended a ground diet and thin liquids due to dysphagia. Urology replaced his suprapubic catheter during admission. He improved clinically, with normalization of labs, and was discharged home on a 10-day course of oral antibiotics with follow-up instructions.
